claims.correct_work_keeps_score: yes: textual witnesses 6.28 old, 6.28 new; bad control 0 on both; real solver rises rather than falls
claims.note: The real solver loses about 6 points to this lookup and sees it on public files too (10 of 12 correct, 12 of 12 with the fix), but the full-set effect is only measurable with a second, unrequested judge fix in place because the shipped judge scores this solver 0 (see new_finding), and all runs used 8 CPUs and 7g against the official 16 and 16g, with 6 to 7 solver OOM kills per run.

new_finding.what: evaluate.py validator recursion overflows the C stack on 5 hard QF_UFLRA files when a solver answers sat; the segfaulting pool worker raises BrokenProcessPool, no score file is written, and the judge reports a valid 0.00 (correct=0/0).
new_finding.evidence: rc -11 on each of the 5 files, 3 of 3 tries, in all 4 per-case runs; rc 0 with a 1 GiB stack; cgroup oom_kill 0 at the crash in direct16-old
new_finding.effect: real unchanged, sforge eval: old lookup 0.00, 0.00 -> [47.04, 46.17] with the stack fix; new lookup 0.00 -> [53.33, 52.1]
new_finding.limit: Measured with 8 CPUs and 7g, not 16 and 16g; the 5 witnesses are then judged invalid and the reason was not recorded; NOTES historical best of 50.43 shows a solver can avoid it, presumably by not answering sat on those files, not measured.
